results.question: In the cross-sectional pilot study of veterans, what cardiac MRI findings in people living with HIV suggested myocardial fibrosis and subclinical dysfunction?
results.answer: In a cross-sectional pilot study of matched veterans, 21 veterans with HIV (mean age 54 years; 71% White, 29% Black) and 20 controls (mean age 56 years; 70% White, 30% Black) were included to explore the relationship between systemic inflammation, myocardial fibrosis, and subclinical cardiac disease in HIV [PMID:41791688]. The study found higher growth differentiation factor (GDF)-15 blood levels, increased extracellular volume, and lower right heart function on MRI among patients with HIV [PMID:41791688]. These findings suggested the presence of increased myocardial fibrosis and subclinical myocardial dysfunction in people living with HIV [PMID:41791688].

results.resolution: Both HIV and control groups are identified (21 versus 20); MRI findings and suggestive, noncausal wording are preserved.

results.question: In the single-arm DYNAMITE study, what structural changes were measured at 9 months and what major adverse cardiac events were observed by 24 months after DynamX implantation?
results.answer: At 9-month follow-up in the DYNAMITE study, mean device area increased to 8.53 ± 1.71 mm2 (absolute difference: 0.37 ± 0.99 mm²; relative difference: 5.52 ± 14.8%, p = 0.010), and mean in-device lumen area decreased to 7.57 ± 1.86 mm2 (absolute difference: -0.70 ± 1.09 mm²; relative difference: -7.98 ± 14.9%, p <0.001) [PMID:41765253]. At 24-month follow-up, 4 patients (7.4%) experienced major adverse cardiac events, including one target vessel myocardial infarction and 4 target lesion revascularization events [PMID:41765253].

results.question: How was SCAR-Net built and validated for distinguishing postoperative breast scars from recurrent lesions, and how much did it change radiologist performance?
results.answer: SCAR-Net is a deep learning model specifically designed for ultrasound-based discrimination between postoperative scars and recurrent lesions in breast cancer [PMID:42023157]. The model was developed using 34,376 ultrasound images from 5,710 patients across four hospitals [PMID:42023157]. SCAR-Net incorporates a scar-recurrence feature enhancer and boundary-sensitive attention network modules [PMID:42023157]. In multicenter validation, SCAR-Net significantly improved radiologists' diagnostic performance by increasing AUC from 0.810-0.824 to 0.939-0.942 [PMID:42023157]. The model increased sensitivity from 0.775-0.782 to 0.934-0.941 and specificity from 0.839-0.872 to 0.935-0.950 [PMID:42023157]. All improvements in AUC, sensitivity, and specificity were statistically significant with p < 0.001 [PMID:42023157].

notes: Development size, both named modules, all radiologist metric ranges and significance are present with the correct single source.

results.resolution: Development size, both named modules, all radiologist metric ranges and significance are present with the correct single source.

results.question: What target-specific tumor-localization evidence was reported for the LGR5 tracer [68Ga]Ga-LTP-02 and for the Nectin4 probes in their respective preclinical models?
results.answer: Dynamic PET imaging revealed considerably higher uptake of [68Ga]Ga-LTP-02 in LGR5-positive A549 xenografts (4.74 ± 0.44 %ID/mL) than in LGR5-negative NCI-H1299 xenografts (0.98 ± 0.08 %ID/mL) [PMID:42000453]. Consistently, the tumor-to-muscle ratio was markedly higher in the A549 xenograft model (4.07 ± 0.07) than in the NCI-H1299 model (0.77 ± 0.10) [PMID:42000453]. Saturation binding assays showed that [68Ga]Ga-LTP-02 exhibited higher binding affinity for LGR5 (Kd = 74.11 ± 24.52 nM) than [68Ga]Ga-LTP-01 (Kd = 153.40 ± 17.14 nM) [PMID:42000453]. [68Ga]Ga-/[18F]AlF-NOTA-DN96 demonstrated excellent stability, high target specificity, and partial hepatobiliary elimination, highlighting their potential as promising PET probes for imaging Nectin4-expressing tumors [PMID:41916034]. The tumor-to-muscle (T/M) ratio increased progressively over time and reached its maximum at 120 min post-injection (p.i.) [PMID:41916034]. Notably, both tracers exhibited increased hepatic uptake accompanied by reduced renal accumulation, indicating a shift toward enhanced hepatobiliary clearance [PMID:41916034].

The Nectin4 positive-versus-negative model uptake contrast is omitted; clearance details do not replace that comparator. Additional binding and clearance claims were checked against both cited abstracts.

results.question: How did AI assistance change diagnostic performance in the simulated prostate-MRI triage workflow and in multicenter breast-ultrasound scar-versus-recurrence assessment?
results.answer: In the simulated prostate-MRI triage workflow, the AI system triaged and diagnosed 195 of 400 (49%; 95% CI: 173, 216) examinations with a sensitivity of 94.7% (95% CI: 89.5, 99.9) and a specificity of 94.7% (95% CI: 90.5, 98.9) [PMID:41960994]. In the simulated prostate-MRI triage workflow, the AI-driven pathway maintained comparable sensitivity (89.0%; 95% CI: 85.0, 93.0; P = .36) but improved specificity by 11.5%, reaching 69.2% (95% CI: 64.4, 74.0; P < .001) [PMID:41960994]. In the multicenter breast-ultrasound scar-versus-recurrence assessment, SCAR-Net significantly improved radiologists' diagnostic performance, increasing AUC from 0.810-0.824 to 0.939-0.942, sensitivity from 0.775-0.782 to 0.934-0.941, and specificity from 0.839-0.872 to 0.935-0.950 (all p < 0.001) [PMID:42023157]. Overall diagnostic accuracy increased with AI assistance to a pooled sensitivity and specificity of 0.79 (95% CI 0.71-0.88) and 0.87 (95% CI 0.82-0.91), respectively [PMC:doc260].

results.question: How did the fMRI acceleration method and the MR anisotropic-diffusion filters address different image-reconstruction problems, and what validation result did each report?
results.answer: The fMRI acceleration method addressed the problem of time-consuming data acquisition by combining through-plane and in-plane acceleration techniques to accelerate image acquisition along two dimensions [PMID:41951145]. The fMRI acceleration method used multiple image-shift strategies and a 2D Hadamard encoding scheme to increase encoding diversity and reduce slice leakage [PMID:41951145]. Validation of the fMRI acceleration method on simulated and experimental data showed a reduction in total scan time while achieving higher signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) in regions of interest (ROI) [PMID:41951145]. The fMRI acceleration method demonstrated potential improvements in activation detection under specific acceleration and encoding conditions compared with conventional reconstruction strategies [PMID:41951145]. The MR anisotropic-diffusion filters addressed the problem of denoising images with high Rice's noise levels by proposing adapted filtering anisotropic diffusion PDE filter models using precise local parameters adjustment [PMID:41903663]. The MR anisotropic-diffusion filters incorporated a robust Rician noise estimator and unbiased variants of filters based on anisotropic diffusion with parameters calculated simultaneously and optimized adaptively through the PSO algorithm [PMID:41903663]. Validation of the MR anisotropic-diffusion filters on synthetic and real MR images provided excellent results compared to some other published methods, demonstrating high performance in noise reduction and preservation of important details [PMID:41903663].

notes: Both methods are linked to the correct papers: through-/in-plane acceleration, image shifts and Hadamard encoding with scan-time/SNR/CNR validation; Rician estimation and adaptive anisotropic filtering with denoising/detail-preservation validation. The additional activation-detection statement is explicitly qualified and supported by the fMRI source.

results.question: What association did the hemodialysis study find between AV-access flow and LV mass, and why can it not establish that lowering access flow will improve cardiac outcomes?
results.answer: In this multicenter cross-sectional study, higher AV-access flow was significantly associated with increased left ventricular mass index (mean difference = 22.83; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.37 to 45.29; p = 0.046), whereas dialysis vintage was not (mean difference = 0.51; 95% CI: -0.41 to 1.45; p = 0.27) [PMID:41644509]. The study enrolled a total of 241 hemodialysis patients who had undergone both transthoracic echocardiography and measurement of AV access flow between April 2014 and January 2024 [PMID:41644509]. The study cannot establish that lowering access flow will improve cardiac outcomes because whether AV access blood flow and the duration of exposure to this flow have independent or interactive effects on cardiac outcomes remains unclear [PMID:41644509].

results.question: In the retrospective vacuum-assisted-birth cohort, which factors were independently associated with assisted vaginal birth, and how did mid/low-pelvic applications differ from perineal applications?
results.answer: A retrospective observational monocentric study was conducted on the cohort of women with singleton pregnancies who delivered vaginally in 2023 at the Fondazione IRCCS Ca' Granda Ospedale Maggiore Policlinico in Milan [PMID:42036403]. A total of 3455 vaginal births were included: 3090 spontaneous vaginal births and 365 assisted vaginal births [PMID:42036403]. After adjusting for all factors considered, maternal age (OR 1.04, 95% CI: 1.01-1.07), mode of conception (OR 1.58, 95% CI: 1.07-2.33), epidural analgesia (OR 6.25, 95% CI: 3.05-12.80), gestational age (OR 1.48, 95% CI: 1.31-1.67), and newborn male sex (OR 1.35, 95% CI: 1.06-1.73) were positively associated with assisted vaginal birth [PMID:42036403]. After adjusting for all factors considered, parity (OR 0.20, 95% CI: 0.14-0.29) was inversely associated with assisted vaginal birth [PMID:42036403]. Compared to perineal applications, mid/low pelvic applications were associated with greater blood loss (p < 0.01) [PMID:42036403]. Compared to perineal applications, mid/low pelvic applications were associated with a higher episiotomy rate (95.5% vs 88.2%, p = 0.03) [PMID:42036403]. Compared to perineal applications, mid/low pelvic applications were associated with increased ultrasound use (62.4% vs 23.5%, p < 0.01) [PMID:42036403].

notes: All requested risk-factor directions and the three application-group differences are preserved, including both percentages and P values. The additional cohort details and odds-ratio confidence intervals match the cited abstract.

results.question: In the prospective thoracic ASRT study, what did online adaptation change in target coverage and organ-at-risk dose, and what treatment-time and toxicity results were reported?
results.answer: In the prospective thoracic ASRT study, online adaptation significantly improved target coverage (median V100% change: +0.1%±2.5%) compared to predicted plans (-2.6%±7.3%, p < 0.001), without significant differences in OAR doses [PMID:42058324]. The median total treatment time was 28 min, with an average 5-minute ASRT workflow [PMID:42058324]. No grade ≥ 3 toxicities were reported; grade 2 events occurred in 10.3% of patients [PMID:42058324].
